bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the break-action take-down as documented in Caesar Guerini’s own over-and-under manual: the take-apart every break-action shotgun is built for. It is not Zoli’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Zoli exists for this model. But a break-action gun is built to come apart into three pieces — stock and action, barrels, fore-end — and that take-down is documented in Caesar Guerini’s own over-and-under manual, which this guide follows. It is the same take-apart whether yours is an over-under, a side-by-side or a single-barrel; where this guide says "each barrel", work every barrel yours has. If your fore-end is held by a screw, the strip stops before it starts.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 12 GA. The gauge and chamber length marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose shell, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Top lever over, barrels down, shells out
steps.action: Push the top lever to the right — on a few guns the opening lever sits elsewhere; work the one yours has — support the action, and let the barrels pivot open. Lift out anything the extractors raise, or catch what the ejectors throw.
steps.quote: Push the top lever to the right, support the receiver with the shooting hand and with the other hand grasp the top of the barrels palm down at the front of the fore-end and push down.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO UNLOAD THE GUN, PDF p.11 (printed p.19)

steps.title: Look through every barrel, feel every chamber — twice
steps.action: Look through each bore from the breech against the light and run a fingertip into every chamber the gun has. Close, open, and do it all a second time. A shell left in a chamber is the one thing this whole guide exists to catch.
steps.quote: Make certain the shotgun is on safe and the action open with shells removed from both barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Close the action again before the strip
steps.action: Odd as it reads, the book closes the empty gun before the fore-end comes off — a closed action cannot drop its barrels early. Close the breech and confirm the top lever has come back to engage.
steps.quote: Close the breech and make sure the top lever engages the barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Fore-end off by its latch — a screw is a stop
steps.action: Find the fore-end’s release: a latch lever on its underside, a button at its tip, or a plain snap-on fit that yields to a firm pull at the front end. Work it and lift the fore-end away from the barrels, onto a soft cloth.
steps.quote: Press down on the fore-end latch and remove the fore-end
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)
steps.warn: If a screw holds the fore-end on, or it will not release by hand, stop here: clean the gun with the fore-end on and the action open. A screw’s torque belongs to the maker.

steps.title: Barrels off the hinge — and that is the whole take-down
steps.action: Open the action with the top lever, keep control of the barrels, and lift them up and off the hinge. Lay them on a soft cloth — never stood on their muzzles. Stock, trigger group (even a drop-out one), ejectors, extractors and anything held by a screw stay exactly as they are: Zoli’s work.
steps.quote: Open the action using the top lever, being careful to keep control of the barrels and carefully remove the barrels from the receiver
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Each bore and chamber, from the breech
steps.action: A patch wet with bore solvent through each bore from the chamber end, then the brush, full strokes all the way through, then dry patches until one comes out clean. A chamber brush on each chamber — plastic wad fouling builds a ring at the chamber mouth that makes shells stick.
steps.quote: Wet a patch with bore cleaning solvent and wet the inside of each bore by pushing the wet patch through from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Chokes stay in — greased, not forgotten
steps.action: Screw-in chokes stay in their muzzles for this clean. They do need coming out now and then with the maker’s wrench so they cannot seize — and when they are out, the book’s own advice is a light film of grease on their walls before they go back.
steps.quote: we recommend covering the external circumference of the choke tube with a light quantity of protective grease.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF CHOKE TUBES, PDF p.11 (printed p.18)

steps.title: Standing breech, outside of the barrels, and the pivots
steps.action: Wipe the standing breech — the flat face with the firing-pin holes — and keep oil out of those holes. Wipe the extractors or ejectors in place at the barrels’ breech end. Wipe the outside of the barrels dry of moisture and residue and leave a protective film on the bluing; then a thin film of grease or oil on the hinge pin, the barrel hooks and the fore-end iron’s bearing face, where metal turns on metal.
steps.quote: Carefully wipe the outside of the barrels to remove any moisture, dirt, carbon or other residues from the bluing.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)
steps.warn: Rust can and will occur if this step is neglected and this is NOT covered by warranty.

steps.title: Receiver brushed, wood kept dry of solvent
steps.action: Brush residue out of the receiver with a soft bristle brush and a little general-purpose solvent, and keep solvent off the wood. Lubricate with a thin film only — enough to stop rust and no more.
steps.quote: The receiver should have any residue/carbon/ dirt removed with a soft bristle brush and general purpose solvent.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK, RECEIVER AND FORE-END GROUP, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the barrels, the action and the stock for cracks, dents or rings in the barrels, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Zoli.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Zoli has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Zoli Kronos, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Zoli exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Zoli, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORES & CHAMBERS
tasks: Each bore wet-patched and brushed from the breech end, then dry patches until clean
Each chamber with a chamber brush — the plastic ring at the mouth
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: ACTION & HINGE
tasks: ⛔ No oil into the firing-pin holes
Extractors or ejectors wiped in place
A thin film of grease or oil on the hinge pin, barrel hooks and fore-end iron

cleaning.name: CHOKES
tasks: Periodic removal with the maker’s wrench so they cannot seize; a light film of grease on the walls when refitted

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Barrels onto the hinge, lever over, breech closed
reassembly.action: Set the barrels’ locking block against the inside of the receiver, confirm the hooks engage the hinge, then move the top lever to the right and close the breech.
reassembly.quote: Make sure this locking block engages in the receiver then move the top lever to the right and close the breech.
reassembly.section: ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, step b, PDF p.12 (printed p.16)

reassembly.title: It is not assembled yet — the warning that matters
reassembly.action: The gun looks whole now, but the book’s own caution is the one every break-action owner learns once: open it before the fore-end is on and the barrels come off in your hands.
reassembly.quote: CAUTION: THOUGH THE GUN IS BASICALLY ASSEMBLED AT THIS TIME, THE BARRELS WILL COME OFF THE RECEIVER IF THE BREECH IS OPENED BEFORE THE FORE-END IS INSTALLED!
reassembly.section: ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, caution after step b, PDF p.12 (printed p.16)

reassembly.title: Fore-end on until the catch snaps
reassembly.action: Fore-end onto the front of the receiver, its front pressed toward the barrels until the catch snaps in. Only then is the gun safe to open.
reassembly.quote: Place the fore-end on the front of the receiver and push the front of the fore-end toward the barrels until the fore-end catch snaps into place (photo 5).
reassembly.section: ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, step c, PDF p.12 (printed p.16)

fncheck: Every chamber proven empty twice. With the fore-end on, open the gun with the top lever and close it again: it opens smoothly, the barrels stay on the receiver, and the lever snaps back toward centre, locking the breech. A safety, if fitted, moves through its positions. This check never asks you to pull a trigger; whether a gun of this kind may be dry-fired, with snap caps or without, is a question for Zoli.
